item.title: Why This Week’s Meeting of World Leaders Won’t Be Yalta 2.0

item.title: The Bitter Feud Between the Leaders of Brazil and Argentina Goes Global
item.description: The insults, snubs and dismissals between the leftist Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Javier Milei are escalating.

item.description: Before departing Washington, Trump said some on his team want friendly ties with China while others want “a blowup.”

item.title: Alice Huang’s Husband Built a Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State
item.description: Kang Wei developed the business while his wife was involved with Nvidia’s then-CEO.

item.title: Nvidia’s Board Not Considering Reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: Billionaire allies have called for his return as inquiries into his relationship with a woman suspected of working with Chinese intelligence proceed.

item.title: Put-Downs, Parties and a ‘Royal Family’: The Culture Inside Jensen Huang’s Nvidia
item.description: The longtime Nvidia boss was known for being demanding and difficult. So was his daughter.

item.title: Oil Falls as Improving Supply Prospects Offset Mideast Tensions
item.description: Oil weakened as improving supply prospects offset Middle East tensions.

item.description: Plus, Trump said he might meet with Kim Jong Un this week, and Kalshi bought a securities firm to expand into stock trading.

item.title: Watch What U.S. Aircraft Carriers Bring to the Iran War
item.description: Wall Street Journal journalists visited the USS George Washington to learn how the warships are taking the fight to Iran.

item.title: Nvidia Scandal Threatens China’s Charm Offensive Ahead of Trump Summit
item.description: The Nvidia spy scandal has engulfed China’s relations with Washington ahead of a gathering with President Trump and Russian leader Vladimir Putin.

item.title: Trump Says He Might Meet With North Korea’s Kim During Asia Trip
item.description: The president met with Kim Jong Un during his first term, first in Singapore, then stepping briefly into North Korea a year later.

item.title: Bank of Canada Gov. Macklem to Leave in June, Kicking Off Search for New Leader
item.description: The decision marks the unofficial start of the race to be Canada’s chief central banker, who would take over as the economy undergoes a transition to reduce its dependence on trade with the U.S. to drive growth.

item.title: UniCredit’s Commerzbank Bid Gets EU, U.S. Approval
item.description: The European Union’s merger regulator approved UniCredit’s bid to take control of Germany’s Commerzbank, clearing a key regulatory hurdle for a takeover that has been two years in the making and previously faced opposition in Berlin.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of November 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Eurozone Industrial Production Picked Up in September
item.description: Eurozone industrial production rebounded in September, offering some relief to the sector, which has struggled to regain momentum amid persistently high energy costs driven by the war in Iran.

item.title: Demand for Chinese Goods Is Soaring but Economic Momentum Slows at Home
item.description: Consumption and investment have weakened, keeping China reliant on exports for growth.

item.title: In the Philippines, Trump Checks In With an Ally Resisting Chinese Aggression
item.description: Chinese forces have been increasingly aggressive in the disputed South China Sea and have clashed with the Philippines, a U.S. ally.

item.title: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, Architect of Mexico’s Modern Drug Trade, Dies at 80
item.description: He united traffickers to form the Guadalajara Cartel, creating a multibillion-dollar business built on political protection and violence.

item.title: Iran Targets Bahrain Again After Resuming Attacks on U.S. Ally
item.description: The island kingdom, repeatedly hit by Tehran since the start of the war, said it destroyed incoming drones.

item.title: China Poached This Top Harvard Professor. Now He Wants Others to Join Him.
item.description: Liu Jun’s journey, from Beijing to Boston and back, exemplifies the exodus of Chinese scholars from the U.S.
